unregistered-this-qualified-escape.note: a CHARGED control: §C{this.onChange} INVOKES the this.-qualified field rather than passing it. Arm B: error Calor0410 'uses effect unknown' plus Calor0411 — invoking is charged, passing as a row-instantiating argument is not. The normative content of #1136 is the MEASUREMENT TABLE, not a sentence: two one-line rules have already been withdrawn ('specific to this.'; 'cannot resolve to a rowed declaration in the enclosing class'), and 'read through an explicit receiver' fails too — a §PROP and an inherited field escape by SIMPLE NAME with no receiver, while a module-qualified module function is charged. Measured on arm B (v0.15.0, no flags), each shape in its own single-fact fixture with no §NEW in the method under test (an allocation adds 'alloc' and produces a Calor0410 that is not about the callback — the artefact that confounded two earlier measurements). CHARGED (error Calor0410, exit 1): module function by simple name; module function module-qualified (in module scope); own rowed §FLD by simple name; static rowed §FLD; a local bound FROM such a field; a §B-bound §LAM with its row omitted. ESCAPES (warning Calor0425, exit 0, still emits): own §FLD via this.; §PROP by simple name; own §FLD via a local alias of this; a §FLD on another instance of the same class; an instance method group with a parameter receiver. An adjudicator applies the table; any gloss is never a substitute for it.

escapeSemantics: result.json escapedBugs = held-out failures at declared-done and heldoutPassed = passes (run-pair.sh extract_metrics; a non-compiling final state counts as ALL tests failing), and taskSuccess is escapedBugs == 0. PP-W-rows does NOT read escapedBugs as its leg-A escape: ESCAPE = at least one of tests.effectObservingTests failed on a workspace that BUILT. A run whose declared-done state does not build — the shape arm B's shortcut takes, and any budget exhaustion — is NOT an escape; it is published as its own category (non-building declared-done), because scoring it as up to heldoutTestCount escapes would invert leg A's sign against the arm whose compiler refuses the laundering.

parity.notes: Both arms are Calor; the starters differ only by effect rows (before/ vs after/). Not a C#-vs-Calor pair; the gates-doc §3.3 decl/complexity parity is trivially equal.

shapeRealizedIndicator.name: observer installed in the field
shapeRealizedIndicator.question: the final source INSTALLS an observer in the §FLD{Action<i32>:onChange:pri} field (a §CTOR assignment), rather than printing directly from Bump
shapeRealizedIndicator.reportedBy: ppw-analyze.py, per cell, beside the escape rate
shapeRealizedIndicator.why: The frozen starter already DECLARES the field, so an indicator keyed on the declaration would read 'shape realized' on a workspace where the agent wrote nothing — vacuous exactly where it is needed, since W-004 is one of the three blind cells the verdict is read on. The starter has no constructor and never installs an observer, so the assignment is what distinguishes a realized cell from one where the agent printed straight from Bump and left the callback unwired — in which case a null escape rate says nothing about rows. Recorded, never scored.
